content: Harden the agent/ guidance so that an agent cannot change this repository without onboarding through its rules: entry-point rules, a cold-start skill, and a pre-commit gate.

AGENTS.md at the repository root becomes the machine entry point: five hard rules (read order, session-before-change, no silent constraint relaxation, verify before commit, record outcomes). Root README and the agent README's new 'Before changing anything' block both point at it.

A start-work skill encodes the cold-start on-ramp: read order, open-decisions check for the task area, skill matching, scaffold-before-change, verification, and finish-through-record-session. It is the fourth skill and the first entry in the skills index.

The pre-commit hook (.githooks/pre-commit, auto-installed by the Nix devshell via core.hooksPath, python3 added to the shells) enforces three things per commit: records validation, the validator self-test (silenced output), and session coverage -- staged changes outside agent/ are rejected while no session is in progress, with the exact scaffold command in the error.

Failure path verified live before committing: staged non-agent changes with no in-progress session were rejected (exit 1) with the scaffold instruction; scaffolding the session made the hook pass; the devshell rebuild succeeded with python3 and the hooksPath wiring; the implementation commit then ran the hook for real.

One usability fix during testing: the self-test invocation was redirected to /dev/null but its stderr still flooded the hook output; both streams are silenced now, keeping the hook's output to the records validator result and any coverage error.
